title: A Bavarian servant to his duke, and a report on the Pressburg talks, c. 1533-34, BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.262-263 (DECODE R9416; catalogue 161)

documents.shelfmark: BayHStA Kurbayern Äußeres Archiv 4591 ff.262-263 (DECODE R9416)
documents.route: Bavarian agent(s) → the Duke of Bavaria

plaintext.source: f.262 fully glossed at the time; f.263 glossed on its first lines only, broken here.

transcription.notes: Length is f.263 only. f.263 one char per sign in r9416/p34_v2.txt (v2 split of look-alikes); f.262 only its gloss transcribed (r9416/gloss.txt).

system.summary: Two sign sets in one record. f.262: homophonic graphic signs, glossed throughout at the time. f.263: a German homophonic substitution with about 23 frequent signs, word-separated ('io' always together), and person codes 'der d', 'der g', 'der h'.
system.sibling_key: none: f.263 broken from the ciphertext; f.262 not keyed
system.notes: f.263 measured 58 distinct transcription codes (v2, with look-alike splits and doubtful signs). Split on 15 Oct 2026 from kaa4591 (catalogue 161).

prior_solution.where: f.262 deciphered at the time (interlinear); a faint gloss over the first lines of f.263, found to agree after the break; no edition found.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie supplied; problem posed with /goal; the user asked for a period German model. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Web search for KAA 4591 and Augurelio ciphers
DECODE record list from the API dump (141 records in the volume); images of the 14 targets and 30 neighbouring keys fetched with the cookie
R9416 f.262 gloss transcribed (read at the time)
Built de-1500s model from 145 Deutsches Textarchiv prints 1472-1609; annealing on R9416 f.263 (3150 signs) gave running German (Pressburg talks, Gritti)
R9416 f.263 re-transcribed splitting look-alike signs found by the solver's errors
Lasry (25 Sept 2026): split mixed cases. Primary method stays key from adjacent plaintext; R9416 f. 263, broken ciphertext-only, is a second part with its own Results row.

R9416 f.263 recto lines 11-16 re-keyed by hand from the v2 transcription and checked word by word on the image: v2 sign z split into e (one-bar zig-zag) and s (two-bar dagger), b into d and l; lines 11-12 agree with the faint contemporary gloss ('das aus den tag zu bresburg erfolgt ist dahin auch / des Ferd tail ... mit grossem bumbb kummen sint auch'). Normalised passage (Pressburg diet, 'mit grossem Pomp', full powers, the Turkish embassy on Shrove Tuesday) in r9416/reading_p3_11-16.txt; rest of f.263 not yet re-keyed.

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from kaa4591 (catalogue 161), whose fourteen records are letters in at least six systems: System A′ stays in kaa4591; Łaski's System B is kaa4591b; R9325 is fulda1576; R9367, R9416, R9424 and R9319 are r9367, r9416, r9424 and r9319; R9291 is a key fragment. R9416 keeps outcome.parts: f.262 and f.263 are two sign sets in one record.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 199 tokens, 25 types, de-1500s order 4: reading -2.667 per letter; polyphonic: 13% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

validation.notes: polyphonic: 13% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value

outcome.method_basis: The f.263 homophonic substitution (3,150 signs) was broken by constrained annealing with the de-1500s model on the first run; the faint gloss on its first lines agrees word for word. f.262 is read from its contemporary decipherment (second part).
outcome.fraction_read_source: mk_validation.py: 199 of the 3,313 transcription codes of f.263 (p34_v2.txt) read clean on recto lines 11-16 (the rest a working decrypt, not counted); a lower bound. f.262 not counted (signs not transcribed)
outcome.notes: f.263: running German with local errors (working decrypt), recto lines 11-16 deciphered clean by hand (30 Sept 2026); codes der d / der g / der h are persons. f.262: the gloss is faint and only partly transcribed.
